text:
rina: hey team, day 1 hiccup. I can browse public sites fine but `curl http://internal.api.redwood.internal/health` returns a 502 from our corporate proxy. `echo $HTTP_PROXY` shows `http://proxy.corp:8080`. Not sure how to bypass proxy for internal hosts. any quick fixes? :grimacing:

it-ops: welcome rina! if your machine is using the corp proxy (Zscaler/BlueCoat/etc.) it will often intercept HTTP(S). internal hosts should be routed direct via VPN though. Quick test: `curl -x "" http://internal.api.redwood.internal/health` (empty proxy) or `curl --noproxy "internal.api.redwood.internal" http://internal.api.redwood.internal/health` — does that work?

rina: tried `curl --noproxy` and it returns the expected JSON 200. so DNS and routing are fine. looks like the system proxy is forcing traffic through the corp proxy and breaking things.

neteng: OK that confirms proxy is the culprit. Two approaches: 1) add internal domains to the NO_PROXY environment variable for CLI tools and processes. Example for bash/zsh: `export NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,.redwood.internal,10.10.0.0/16` (note some tools don't support CIDR in NO_PROXY). 2) Add proxy exceptions in the OS proxy settings so GUI apps and system services bypass the proxy for `*.redwood.internal`. Which OS are you on?

rina: macOS Ventura. If I change NO_PROXY in my shell it works for curl, but VS Code terminal still goes through proxy and docker still fails. How do I update system proxy exceptions?

it-ops: on macOS: System Settings -> Network -> [your active interface] -> Advanced -> Proxies. If you're configured with an automatic proxy configuration (PAC) script, you need to edit the PAC to include a `shExpMatch(host, "*.redwood.internal")` bypass or add an explicit bypass list. For manual proxies, add `*.redwood.internal` to the "Bypass proxy settings for these Hosts & Domains" list. If your laptop is managed by MDM, the proxy may be pushed by config profile; ping us if the setting is locked.

jamie: for Docker Desktop specifically, Docker has its own proxy environment for the daemon. Go to Docker Desktop -> Settings -> Resources -> Proxies and add the no-proxy entries there (e.g., `internal.registry.redwood.internal,*.redwood.internal,10.10.0.0/16`). Also restart Docker after making changes.

devex: other gotchas: git and tooling sometimes read `http.proxy` in git config. Check `git config --global --get http.proxy`. If set, you can add per-repo overrides: `git -c http.proxy= clone ...` or unset globally with `git config --global --unset http.proxy`. For Maven/Gradle also check their proxy config files; they may not honor NO_PROXY.

rina: ok I removed git http.proxy and added NO_PROXY in my shell. Docker Desktop still hit the proxy until I added the bypass in Docker settings and restarted. VS Code integrated terminal still used the proxy until I launched VS Code from terminal after exporting NO_PROXY — looks like GUI apps inherit environment only when started from login shell.

neteng: good learnings. We'll add these steps to onboarding docs: a) check system proxy/PAC exceptions for `*.redwood.internal`; b) set NO_PROXY for CLI tools and persist it for your shell; c) update Docker Desktop and other apps with explicit no-proxy lists; d) check git/maven/gradle specific proxy configs. We'll also document how to test quickly with `curl --noproxy` and `env | grep -i proxy`.

jamie: one more edge-case: corporate PAC scripts occasionally include a proxy fallback that still returns a 502 for private IPs even if PAC says DIRECT (we saw this with older PACs). If you hit that, open a ticket and IT can whitelist the internal DNS zones at the proxy edge or adjust the PAC logic.

devex-bot: created ticket #INFR-4410 to add "Proxy bypass for internal hosts" to the new-hire VPN checklist and onboarding docs (include macOS, Windows, Docker Desktop, git hints and test commands).

rina: thanks everyone  everything working now after the Docker + system bypass changes. leaving a tiny summary for new-hires: if internal services return proxy 502s, try `curl --noproxy`, set NO_PROXY for your shell, update Docker Desktop and system proxy exceptions for `*.redwood.internal`. saved my morning. :tada:
